text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Syrian newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara: "U.S. has no right to dispose with Israel's commitment on Golan pullout. Peace talks between Syria and Israel talks should resume from the point at which they stopped."
- South Africa will set up strong ties with Arabs, Vice-President Mbeki says.
- Israeli provocations, oppression against Golan citizens escalate.
- EU envoy in Damascus on Monday.
- U.S. senate approves Albright as Secretary of State.
- France stresses Europe's role in the Middle East.
- Halt to Jewish settlement building demanded by Palestinian Authority.
- Amid American threats South Africa stresses determination to promote ties with Arabs.. says "we do not care about U.S. pressure and will sell arms to Syria."
- Four earthquakes hit region. no casualties or material damage in Syria.

- Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu renews call for talks without pre-conditions...says "we want the whole of the Golan." Lebanese Prime Minister Hariri says: "Netanyahu is hostile to peace and is not trustworthy.
- South Africa continues its criticism of the U.S. stand and says will continue measures to conclude arms deal with Syria.
- Arab financial aid to developing countries totals $103 billion in 25 years.
- Lebanon renews rejection of Israeli proposals for peace.
- Arab parliamentarians to hold seminar in Damascus on the strategic importance of water in the Arab world.
